title: Mountain View
name: Mountain View
metaTitle: Mountain View 1031 Exchange Investors | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange guidance for Mountain View investors weighing North Bayshore office campuses, the district's housing rezoning, and Castro Street's walkable retail.

sections.html: Mountain View's North Bayshore district reads as one continuous Google campus from the street, but the city has spent years rezoning parts of that same district for housing, and an exchanger evaluating property there needs to know which side of that shift a given parcel sits on. That distinction matters more here than in most South Bay cities, since North Bayshore's zoning has genuinely moved in the years since many exchangers last looked closely at the district.

sections.heading: North Bayshore Is Half Office Campus, Half Housing Experiment
sections.html:
Google's campuses dominate North Bayshore's identity, with LinkedIn and other tech tenants filling out the rest of the district along Shoreline Boulevard. For years the area was zoned almost entirely for office and R&D use.

The city has since approved housing in parts of North Bayshore that were previously office-only, and that rezoning changes the highest-and-best-use math for any parcel nearby. An exchanger should confirm current zoning directly rather than assuming a neighboring office campus locks in the same use for every adjacent parcel.

sections.heading: Two Corridors, Two Different Buyer Pools
sections.html:
A realistic Mountain View shortlist spans a few distinct categories:

  • single-tenant NNN office and R&D campuses in North Bayshore, leased to major tech tenants
  • emerging multifamily parcels in the rezoned portions of North Bayshore
  • downtown Castro Street retail and restaurant space, walkable to the Caltrain station
  • older garden-style apartments competing with newer transit-oriented supply
  • light-industrial and flex buildings near the Moffett Field boundary

sections.heading: Shoreline Amphitheatre Traffic Is Seasonal, Not Constant
sections.html:
Shoreline Amphitheatre draws real crowds on concert nights through the warmer months, and nearby hospitality and retail leases sometimes lean on that seasonal traffic as part of their pitch.

The venue's calendar is concentrated in a few months a year, and a lease priced on peak-season visibility rather than average annual demand is pricing the exception. Ask for trailing sales across a full year before treating amphitheatre proximity as a durable advantage.

sections.heading: Castro Street's Walkability Commands a Real Premium
sections.html:
Downtown Mountain View's Castro Street corridor has built a genuine walkable retail identity around the Caltrain station, distinct from the office-park character of North Bayshore just a mile away.

That walkability supports higher rents, but it also means Castro Street retail competes on foot traffic and tenant mix rather than the tech-employer proximity that drives North Bayshore leasing. An exchanger should underwrite each corridor on its own terms rather than assuming Mountain View trades as one uniform market. A downtown storefront's actual sales history matters far more here than any citywide reputation for tech-driven demand.

sections.heading: Zoning Ambiguity Belongs in the File Early
sections.html:
A North Bayshore parcel near the housing-rezoning boundary needs the qualified intermediary, the tax advisor, and a lender who understands the current zoning status, all reviewing the same file before the identification notice goes out. The same caution applies to light-industrial parcels near the Moffett Field boundary, where federal-adjacent restrictions can add another layer to the zoning question.

Skip that coordination and the risk is direct: a lender treats an ambiguous-zoning parcel as higher risk than expected, financing stalls, and the 180-day window closes with the gain still due. Confirm figures and deadlines with your own advisors directly; this page describes the market, not tax advice.

faqs.q: Does an address in North Bayshore guarantee office-zoned use?
faqs.a: No. Confirm current zoning directly, since the city has rezoned parts of the district for housing in recent years.

faqs.q: Is Shoreline Amphitheatre proximity a reliable retail advantage?
faqs.a: Only if trailing sales hold up across the full year rather than only the concert season, since the venue's calendar is concentrated in a few months.

faqs.q: Can I identify more than one Mountain View property?
faqs.a: Yes. Up to three regardless of value under the standard rule, or more under the 200% rule if combined value stays within twice what you sold.

faqs.q: Should I underwrite Castro Street retail the same way as North Bayshore office?
faqs.a: No, they compete on different terms — foot traffic and tenant mix downtown versus tech-employer proximity in North Bayshore.

faqs.q: What if my Mountain View identification falls through near Day 45?
faqs.a: Have a genuinely underwritten backup ready and avoid taking receipt of exchange funds while you sort it out.

faqs.q: Are light-industrial parcels near Moffett Field treated like standard industrial property?
faqs.a: Not always. Some carry additional restrictions tied to the adjacent federal property, so confirm any use limitations directly with the city before assuming standard industrial zoning applies.

faqs.q: Does Mountain View's multifamily perform the same across the whole city?
faqs.a: No. Newer transit-oriented product near Caltrain and North Bayshore competes on different terms than older garden-style complexes farther from those corridors, so compare them as separate tiers.

faqs.q: Should I weight a North Bayshore office building's value on its Google-area address alone?
faqs.a: No. Confirm the specific tenant, lease term, and whether the parcel sits in a zone the city has already targeted for future housing conversion.

faqs.q: How far in advance should I confirm zoning on a North Bayshore parcel?
faqs.a: As early as possible, ideally before you even shortlist the property. Zoning confirmation can take longer than expected in a district actively being rezoned, and a lender may not move forward until that status is resolved in writing.

faqs.q: Do older Mountain View apartment buildings need any special diligence beyond the usual inspection?
faqs.a: Check for deferred maintenance and any local rent-stabilization rules that may apply to older units, since those rules can affect achievable rent growth in ways a simple physical inspection won't reveal on its own.
